author: FOX 23 Tulsa KOKI
title: Teach for America hosts educational leadership breakfast discussing education outcomes - NewsBreak
text:
12 hours ago TULSA, Okla. — Teach for America Greater Tulsa hosted its annual educational leadership breakfast discussing the group's progress toward improving educational standards in Oklahoma.
The annual Rise and Shine Breakfast was held at the Discovery Lab and featured speakers from Teach for America, Monroe Demonstration Academy and McClain High School.
"Today we're here to celebrate Teach for America's impact in greater Tulsa," shared Teach for America's CEO Aneesh Sohoni. "We've been here since 2009 working with the community to find incredible leaders who are in college or early in their career who commit to spending at least two years in the classroom and then use that experience to both help students achieve incredible academic outcomes, feel motivated to engage in their education and then also make a lifelong impact serving as principals or leaders of nonprofits all across greater Tulsa."
Sohoni said educational leaders are now more important than ever in Oklahoma.
"I'm sure many people have seen the data and the statistics showing that Oklahoma ranks oftentimes in the bottom five states in terms of educational outcomes, but what we know is that it doesn't have to be that way. Something that I'm inspired by is the conversation I heard here today by leaders and community partners coming together to say we're going to show that a different future is possible because the future that we have today is unacceptable for our students, but we're going to work at creating a better future for everyone."
Events like the educational breakfast allow individuals throughout various school systems to gather and discuss these issues with one another.
"We also talked a lot about how our network comes together to solve really hard problems. Teach for America creates space for them to come together in ways that they may not otherwise have the time or ability to. The power of bringing people together to have really important conversations about where greater Tulsa needs to go next in terms of its educational outcomes is a powerful role that we play as well."
Sohoni said one of the first steps to improving education for students is to truly believe in them and their capability to be excellent.
"One of the things that I think a lot about is the power of holding a set of high expectations for all students. What we know and what we've seen time and time again is when you hold a high bar for students, students meet that bar. Something that I think the Teach for America network here does so well is to create a standard of excellence for all students no matter what zip code they come from."
